scenes.title: Scene 1: Why
scenes.spoken: Jono, this film is about one button in the broker portal: Connect my Outlook calendar. Here's what it does. A SortMyCover lead is routed to a broker, say Mark, while his order has leads left. Our assistant offers only times when Mark is really free in Outlook. The client picks one, and the meeting lands in Mark's own calendar, with a Teams link. The invite reaches the client from Mark's own email address, because his calendar sends it. If the client moves or cancels, the same meeting moves or is removed. One honest note. This booking flow is built, but not switched on yet. It's waiting for its gate test, and a connected calendar lets us run it.

scenes.title: Scene 2: The big picture
scenes.spoken: Here's the whole idea, Jono. You register one app with Microsoft, once. It's called Lead Velocity, and every broker shares it. A broker taps Connect my Outlook calendar and signs in with their work account. Microsoft asks if Lead Velocity may use their calendar. They tap Accept, and they're connected. No broker ever registers anything.

scenes.title: Scene 3: Register the app
scenes.spoken: Sign in at entra dot microsoft dot com as jono at vantage stack dot co dot za. Open Entra I D, then App registrations, then New registration. Type the name, Lead Velocity. Under Supported account types, choose Multiple Entra I D tenants. That lets any company's work account connect. Don't choose personal accounts, because they can't make Teams meetings. Click Register. Now open Authentication and add a redirect address. Choose Web, paste the address on screen exactly, and click Configure. Then add a second Web address, lead velocity dot co dot za slash broker slash calendar. That's where an I T admin lands after approving.

scenes.title: Scene 4: Permissions
scenes.spoken: Next, API permissions. Click Add a permission, then Microsoft Graph, then Delegated permissions. Delegated means the app only ever acts for the broker who signed in. Tick five boxes. open I D signs them in. offline access keeps the connection alive, so they aren't asked again every hour. User dot Read reads their name and email. Calendars dot Read Write sees when they're free and puts bookings in their calendar. Online Meetings dot Read Write makes the Teams link. Click Add permissions. There's no mail permission, and we don't want one. Lead Velocity never reads a broker's email. And don't click Grant admin consent. That only covers your own company.

scenes.title: Scene 5: The secret and the ID
scenes.spoken: Now Certificates and secrets. Under Client secrets, click New client secret. Call it Lead Velocity portal, choose 24 months, which is the longest Microsoft allows, and click Add. Copy the Value straight away. Not the Secret I D, the Value. Microsoft shows it once. Leave the page and it's gone, and you'd have to make a new one. Then go back to Overview and copy the Application, client, I D. That one isn't secret. It just names the app.

scenes.title: Scene 6: Make it look trustworthy
scenes.spoken: Open Branding and properties. This is what brokers see on the Microsoft screen, so it should look like us. Upload the Lead Velocity logo. Microsoft wants a square P N G, 215 by 215 pixels, on a solid background, under 100 kilobytes. Set the home page to lead velocity dot co dot za. Microsoft also asks for a terms of service link and a privacy statement link. Those pages aren't built on our site yet, so leave those two boxes empty for now. Claude will build them, then you paste the links. Click Save.

scenes.title: Scene 7: Hand it to Claude
scenes.spoken: Now hand Claude two things: the Application I D and the secret Value. Never paste the secret into a chat, an email or WhatsApp. Option one: open the file Claude names on screen, paste both values, and save. That file never goes into git. Option two: set them yourself with supabase secrets set. Either way, Claude does the rest. It sets the redirect address, the state secret and the portal address, deploys the sign-in function, and notes the date the secret expires.

scenes.title: Scene 8: What a broker sees
scenes.spoken: Here's what Mark will see. He taps the Microsoft button on his calendar card and picks his work account. Microsoft shows Permissions requested, with Lead Velocity and what it may do. He taps Accept and lands back in the portal, which says Connected, with his next free slot. Some companies stop staff from approving new apps. Then Microsoft says Need admin approval. The portal gives Mark a short note for his I T admin, with a one-click approval link. The admin opens it and accepts for the whole company. Mark taps connect again, and he's done. If I T is slow, he can use our shared calendar for now.

scenes.title: Scene 9: Test it, then Mark
scenes.spoken: Test it on yourself first. Set up a test broker with your own work account, on a SortMyCover order. Without an order, the card says Not available yet. Connect it. When Claude switches the booking flow on for the gate test, book a test meeting like a client would. Check that only free times were offered, that the meeting is in Outlook with a Teams link, and that the invite came from your own address. Then move it, cancel it, and watch Outlook follow. To check any broker from the CRM, open Broker Management, choose the broker, and tap Preview portal. The Appointments tab shows their calendar card. When your test passes, it's Mark's turn.

scenes.title: Scene 10: Later
scenes.spoken: Two things for later. First, publisher verification. Until it's done, Microsoft labels the app unverified, and more companies block it. You'll need a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program account. Then, in Branding and properties, add the Partner I D and verify it. Brokers then see a blue verified badge. Second, Google Calendar, for brokers who don't use Outlook. That isn't built yet. For now, the job is simple, Jono. Register the app, hand Claude the two values, and get Mark connected.
